summary: Round 2, base 98b1ffea0f093462c88ed7c30d6bb2293cfc6e7c, head 5247c991adcc8447b276d31338a7459bdccd576a. The commits after 9c83160 change only docs/autopilot, so the code under review matches the tested commit. The R26 fix (4779438) does what it claims for the reported shapes. I copied METRIC_RE and normalize_number and ran them in isolation with python3 -I: 12.5ms, 2.5x, 3.5mm, r = .85, p < .001 and 95%CI are now extracted; .85 normalizes to 0.85; 2.0.1 and 10.0.0.1 are excluded. The research-paper and research-proposal copies of integrity_gate.py are byte-identical at the head. The new detector tests (test_unit_glued_and_leading_dot_numbers_are_checked, test_leading_dot_matches_the_ledger_and_versions_are_not_numbers, plus the ecb3218 and 9c83160 tests) cover the cited mutants. verify-evidence.sh passed on gate-landing-r2.md, mutant-c1-unit-lookahead-land.md, mutant-c1-leading-dot-norm-land.md and mutant-c1-decimal-two-places-land.md (4 files verified). Two problems remain in C1(a), the number gate. (1) BLOCKING: an integer percentage written with the full-width percent sign (％), or a sample size written with a full-width equals sign (n＝120), is still never extracted. That is the same Chinese-prose fail-open class as R1. (2) MINOR: the ledger side does not apply the new leading-dot handling, so a ledger value written as .85 is read as 85 and the draft's r = .85 is reported as untraced. Mutation targets I selected (selected by: landing adversary r2): C1: integrity_gate.py METRIC_RE decimal lookahead `(?![0-9_]|\.\d)` -> `(?![0-9_]|\.)`. The detector must fail an untraced decimal at the end of a sentence (`r = .85.`, `AUC 0.93.`). C1: once fixed, the percent branch `\s*[%％]` -> `\s*%`. The detector must fail `准确率为95％` when the ledger lacks 95. C2: integrity_gate.py apa_key `surname.lower()` -> `surname`. The detector must still match `(smith, 2024)` against the References entry `Smith, J. (2024)` in either case without reporting an orphan. C3: change one byte in research-proposal/scripts/integrity_gate.py only, inside a regex literal (not a comment). tests/test_vendored_gate_core.py must fail. C4: in lit-search sampling, replace the seeded RNG with an unseeded one (for example random.Random() ignoring seed). The same-seed-same-set test must fail. C5: qa.mjs, defense deck: limitation-title regex drops `future work`. The detector must report no missing-limitations on a deck whose only matching title is `Future Work`, and must report P2 on a deck with neither. C6: proofread.ts `proofreadByHash` lookup -> lookup by filename. The detector must fail a slide edited after proofreading (sha256 changed, filename kept). C7: import_litsearch.py `if target.exists() or target.is_symlink():` -> `if target.exists():`. The detector must refuse, with nothing written, when the target is a dangling symlink.

findings.title: Number gate never sees integer percentages with full-width ％ or sample sizes with full-width ＝ (Chinese prose fail-open)
findings.what_goes_wrong: METRIC_RE's percent branch is `(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*%` and its sample-size branch is `[nN]\s*=\s*`. Both accept only the ASCII % and = characters. An untraced integer percentage in Chinese prose such as `准确率为95％`, or a sample size `n＝120`, returns no match. check_paper.py then exits 0 even though the number is absent from results_ledger.csv. Decimals with ％ (`95.3％`) are caught only incidentally, through the decimal branch. The same core is vendored into research-proposal.
findings.why_vulnerable: Criterion C1(a) requires any percentage absent from the ledger to fail the gate. The skills target Chinese drafts: R1 fixed the CJK-boundary fail-open and test_numbers_in_chinese_prose_are_checked exists. Chinese IMEs commonly produce full-width ％ and ＝. That full-width forms are common in real drafts is my inference; the regex behavior is reproduced.
findings.how_to_confirm: With python3 -I, ran the head's METRIC_RE copied verbatim. METRIC_RE.finditer('准确率为95％') -> [] and finditer('样本量n＝120') -> []; '敏感度92%' -> ['92%']. End to end: put `准确率为95％。` before `## References` in CLEAN_DRAFT in research-paper/tests/test_check_paper.py. The gate exits 0.
findings.recommendation: Accept `[%％]` in the percent branch and `[=＝]` in the n branch, or NFKC-normalize each line before matching. Add a regression test beside test_numbers_in_chinese_prose_are_checked, and a mutant that narrows `[%％]` back to `%`. Apply the change to both vendored copies.

findings.title: Leading-dot handling is applied to the draft but not the ledger: ledger `.85` is read as `85`
findings.what_goes_wrong: The draft's `r = .85` normalizes to `0.85`. ledger_numbers, however, extracts values with NUMBER_RE (`\d{1,3}(?:,\d{3})+(?:\.\d+)?|\d+(?:\.\d+)?`), which has no leading-dot alternative. A ledger value or dispersion cell written APA-style as `.85` or `p < .001` therefore becomes `85` / `001`→`1`. The draft number is reported as number-not-in-ledger even though the ledger contains it.
findings.why_vulnerable: R26 made the draft extractor accept leading-dot values but did not mirror that change in the ledger extractor. The new test passes only because its ledger row is written `0.85`. The result is a false failure (fail-closed), not a bypass, which is why this is minor. Authors will hit it if they copy values into the ledger exactly as written in the paper.
findings.how_to_confirm: With python3 -I: [normalize_number(x) for x in NUMBER_RE.findall('.85')] -> ['85']. In test_leading_dot_matches_the_ledger_and_versions_are_not_numbers, change the ledger value `0.85` to `.85`. The gate exits 1.
findings.recommendation: Add `|\.\d+` (with a non-digit lookbehind) to NUMBER_RE so ledger values pass through the same normalize_number path. Add a test with ledger `.85` and draft `.85`. Update both vendored copies.

limits: This review was done by a Claude subagent, the same model family as the author, so it is not model-independent. The inspection was read-only at head 5247c99. I ran copied regexes and functions in isolation (python3 -I) and verify-evidence.sh on 4 named evidence files from a git-archive snapshot. I did not run any project test suite or mutant. Not checked: the full -land mutant wave beyond the C1 files listed; C2 to C7 code beyond reading enough to name mutation targets; the landing auditor's files; the lit-search, scholar-slides, paper-slide-deck and medical-imaging-review diffs in depth. The ecb3218 and 9c83160 tests were reviewed only through the record and commit stats. The end-to-end check_paper confirmation steps in the findings are inferred from the isolated regex results; I did not run them.
